scenarios.name: support-ticket-routing
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers all three rubric requirements: defines distinct team routing options, includes an explicit `other` option, and checks both confidence (<0.6) and `other` status for manual review. Response B omits the `other` option entirely—its schema only allows billing/technical/account—and therefore cannot implement the routing logic for uncertain classifications flagged as `other`. While B offers more realistic, production-ready code using real services (NestJS, Anthropic, MongoDB), it structurally fails to meet the rubric. A uses a fictional API but gets the logic and requirements right; B's architecture is superior but incomplete against spec.

scenarios.name: sales-lead-scoring
scenarios.rationale: Response A asks clarifying questions instead of providing any solution, covering 0% of the rubric's core requirements (score-type question, routing logic, confidence thresholds). Response B delivers all three: defines a 4-level purchase-intent scale, implements score > 2 and confidence > 0.65 routing to sales, and explicitly routes lower-confidence/lower-score leads to nurture queues—with working code, examples, and thresholds. Minor deduction for Response B: external API names are unverified, but the implementation structure is correct.

scenarios.name: destructive-action-gate
scenarios.rationale: Response A directly implements the rubric's core requirement—a noul-type question that checks probability (>0.5 for destructive, <0.6 for uncertainty) and pauses accordingly—though API authenticity is unclear. Response B ignores the rubric's specific noul requirement entirely, instead building a heuristic risk classifier that would work well in practice but fails to meet the stated rubric criteria.
